subject: why does simple logistic regression cause INLA crash depending on n (sample size)?

messages.author: 778bd0cef6c473fc
messages.subject: why does simple logistic regression cause INLA crash depending on n (sample size)?
parts:
I am trying to run a simple logistic regression, no random effects, nothing special (see code below)

For n=10000, it runs perfectly as expected.

For n=50000, INLA crashes.  

Why is this happening? Is it an issue with one of the control functions, or something else? 

Your insights would be greatly appreciated.

#This code runs:

rm(list=ls())

 

#install.packages("INLA", repos="http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/R/testing")

library(INLA)

 

### Generate data and fit a logistic regression model

n=10000

a = 1

b = 1

z = rnorm(n)

eta = a + b*z

prob = exp(eta)/(1 + exp(eta))

y = rbinom(n, size=1, prob = prob)

 

data = list(y=y,z=z)

formula = y ~ 1+z

result = inla(formula, family = "binomial", data = data, Ntrials=1)

summary(result)


### Does Ntrials argument matter?

result = inla(formula, family = "binomial", data = data)

summary(result)

I have no answer. It runs perfectly fine, even for higher n, here. for
linux/mac and windows. 

sometimes, windows can have little ram available, which can cause the
crash, as the program stops if it doesn't get the memory it need. you
might check this adding

inla(..., num.threads=1)

which runs on 1 cpu, as this requires less memory. 

also, restarting your machine and the retry immediately, could verify
this, as there should be more mem avail then. 

let me know how it goes,
H


PS: if you running a 32bit R, then you probably want to reinstall the
64 bit, which also could cause problems for larger n.
